title: #007. Markowitz Minimum-Variance Portfolio (QP)
subtitle: Minimize quadratic covariance risk w^T Sigma w subject to return and budget constraints.
markdown:
# #007. Markowitz Minimum-Variance Portfolio (QP)

<!-- section:scenario -->
Allocate capital across $n$ risky assets with non-negative portfolio weights $w_i \in [0, \text{maxWeights}[i]]$ summing to `1.0` ($\sum_i w_i = 1$, no short selling). Asset $i$ has expected return `expectedReturns[i]`, and asset pairs $(i, j)$ have symmetric positive-definite covariance matrix `covariance[i][j]`.

Achieve at least the target portfolio return $\sum_i \mu_i w_i \ge r_{\min}$ while **minimizing portfolio variance**:

$$
\min_{w} \; w^\top \Sigma w = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \Sigma_{ij} w_i w_j
$$

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P007Input`)**:
  - `expectedReturns: number[]` — expected return $\mu_i$ of each asset
  - `covariance: number[][]` — $n \times n$ symmetric positive-definite covariance matrix $\Sigma$
  - `maxWeights: number[]` — maximum weight allowed per asset
  - `minReturn: number` — required minimum portfolio expected return $r_{\min}$
- **Output (`P007Output`)**:
  - `weights: number[]` — optimal portfolio allocation vector summing to `1`
  - `variance: number` — minimum portfolio variance $w^\top \Sigma w$

<!-- section:example -->
For 3 assets (`expectedReturns = [0.05, 0.10, 0.14]`, `minReturn = 0.09`, `maxWeights = [0.8, 0.8, 0.8]`):

- Naive asset-picking concentrates in asset 1 alone (`w = [0, 1, 0]` violates the `0.8` cap, or `[0.2, 0.8, 0]` gives variance `0.0624`).
- Diversifying across all three correlated assets drops variance nearly in half to **`variance = 0.033443`** (`weights ≈ [0.422, 0.301, 0.277]`).

<!-- section:hint1 -->
How you express a quadratic objective differs sharply between WaSHI and `highspy`:
- **WaSHI (`TypeScript`)**: Use `QuadExpr` via `weights[i].mul(weights[j]).mul(cov[i][j])` accumulated with `.add(...)` and `m.objective(minimize(variance))`! Note that `sum()` is for linear expressions only and rejects quadratic products.
- **Python (`highspy`)**: `h.minimize(w0 * w0)` raises *"Only linear expressions are allowed"*! Instead, configure `highspy.HighsHessian()` and call `h.passHessian(hess)` followed by `h.run()`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Remember the **`1/2` factor** in `highspy` QP! HiGHS minimizes $\frac{1}{2} x^\top Q x$, whereas our variance objective is $w^\top \Sigma w$:
- Pass **`Q = 2 * cov`** in lower-triangular Compressed Sparse Column (CSC) format (`r >= c`) to `hess.start_`, `hess.index_`, `hess.value_`, set `hess.dim_ = n`, `hess.format_ = highspy.HessianFormat.kTriangular`, call `h.passHessian(hess)`, and solve with `h.run()`!

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{w} \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \Sigma_{ij} w_i w_j \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} w_i = 1 \\
& \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \mu_i w_i \ge r_{\min} \\
& 0 \le w_i \le w_{\max, i} && \forall i
\end{aligned}
$$

When $\Sigma \succ 0$ is positive semidefinite, this quadratic program (QP) is strictly convex — a local minimum is guaranteed to be the unique global minimum!

judge.m0: Output must be an object { weights, variance }.
judge.m1: weights[{p0}] cannot be negative (no short selling; received {p1}).
judge.m4: Expected portfolio return ({p0}%) is below minReturn ({p1}%).
judge.m5: Reported variance ({p0}) does not match w^T Sigma w ({p1}). Tip: did you pass Q = 2 * cov to HighsHessian?
judge.m6: Return target met, but variance ({p0}) exceeds minimum ({p1}).
